title: New Born by Ella Hickson starring Sepideh Moafi, Marianna Gailus, and...
transcript: A mother's all-consuming new connection, a young bartender's missing friend, and a lumberjack’s newfound curiosity for love are all on the menu in New Born by Ella Hickson. This trio of standalone monologues, tied together by the thinnest of threads that's only evident with the help of the piece's title, features Sepideh Moafi, Marianna Gailus, and Hugh Jackman. My experience was a mixed bag, but the episodic nature of the show kept me distracted from one of the tightest theater seats I've ever been in — tall people, beware. I thought the first monologue was dull and poorly written, exacerbated by a wildly unrealistic story and completely forced themes. Despite the fact that I thought it was awful and frankly hard to come back from, it only lasted around 35 minutes and was followed by a stellar middle act. Set in the 1800s, the second monologue was the darkest, the most interesting, and the most well-performed. The final monologue was also enjoyable, though heavily reliant on Hugh Jackman's natural charisma to allow you to fully invest in the character. Neither he nor his material are doing anything particularly innovative here, but he's undeniably easy to watch. I can't see a strong case for putting these specific stories together other than to construct a piece of substantial length, but I enjoyed the variability the evening provided and will be on the lookout for whatever Marianna Gailus is performing in next. With that, another program for my collection.
